transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Kamala (Redwood AE), Liam & Sanjay (Redwood SEs), Mira (Head of ML - Stratagem), Jonas (Platform), Evelyn (CTO), Diego (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Discovery on p95 targets and tokenflow characteristics; customer leaning towards Dedicated for initial pilot but evaluating Hybrid with Hosted fallbacks.
- Need to validate streaming p95 at 250ms for 4 concurrent streams and sustained 800 tokens/sec burst workload.
- Next: send benchmark harness, schedule Dedicated trial, share security docs.

Topics: p95 latency goals, concurrency & streaming behavior, token/sec benchmarking, hosted vs dedicated vs private, caching and batching strategies, security questions (SOC 2, SSO, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Kamala (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, this is Kamala from Redwood. With me is Liam and Sanjay on the technical side. How are you folks doing?
[00:06] Mira (Stratagem): Doing well, thanks. Busy week for us but excited.
[00:09] Evelyn (Stratagem): Hi. We'll try to keep this tight — have a few constraints to run through.
[00:13] Kamala: Totally. Want to start with quick context: you're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference, primarily for streaming tokenized responses in our conversational agent, right?
[00:21] Jonas (Stratagem): Yup. We're shipping an assistant that drives operational playbooks for network ops. It needs to be near realtime, and the p95 on user-facing streams is critical — we have to keep it under about 250–350ms for the accept path.
[00:33] Liam (Redwood SE): Ok got it. When you say 250–350ms p95, is that per-token or end-to-end first-byte on the stream?
[00:40] Mira: Good question. Target is p95 first-token latency for streaming (first token emitted). Then steady-state throughput of tokens/sec after initial chunk should sustain the pacing — we often see bursts around 700–900 tokens/sec for short windows when multiple agents run concurrently.
[00:56] Sanjay: When you say bursts — are those concurrent users or background batch jobs?
[00:59] Mira: Concurrent end-users. Typically 3–6 concurrent active chats per cluster region during incident surges. We want to size for 4 concurrent heavy streams as the baseline for the pilot.
[01:09] Diego (SRE): Also note network egress policy — in some regions our traffic must stay in our VPC, so private deployment is a real option.
[01:15] Kamala: Makes sense. Quick qual — what's the model family you plan to serve? Open weights? LLM provider?
[01:21] Jonas: We're using an open decoder model — 30B-ish, finetuned in-house. We want full control over weights for compliance, so private or dedicated preferred. But if hosted can meet latency/cost we might start there.
[01:33] Liam: Ok, that's useful. For a 30B decoder, p95 first-token of 250ms is ambitious on hosted unless we use smaller context windows, aggressive kv cache, and batching tuned for streaming. Dedicated gives more deterministic p95 because of reserved GPU pools.
[01:47] Evelyn: Cost is a factor too. We prefer predictable ops spend. If dedicated has lower unit-cost and better p95, that's attractive. But our security team will want SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS integration for keys — so private may be the long-term ambition.
[02:01] Kamala: Understood. Let's walk through how Redwood handles streaming and the knobs that affect p95. Liam?
[02:06] Liam: Sure. At a high level: our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache so subsequent tokens after the first are faster. For first-token — it depends on model load, warm vs cold start, and RPC overhead. We also expose model variants and quantization profiles. For Dedicated we pin a model shard to a GPU pool to avoid noisy neighbors. For Private we support customer-managed control plane with KMS and private networking.
[02:27] Jonas: When you say quantization: any regressions on hallucination/quality? We can't sacrifice answer quality.
[02:33] Sanjay: We have a quantization ladder — FP16 -> 8-bit -> 4-bit— and we benchmark quality per-task. For many instruction-following tasks, 8-bit has minimal quality delta; 4-bit sometimes needs tuning. We'll share the eval curves.
[02:44] Mira: Ok. On streaming we saw in our internal tests that the first-token latency spiked with batch sizes > 1. Our UX needs immediate feedback. How do you prioritize single-stream latency vs throughput across tenants?
[02:56] Liam: We can prioritize low-latency skinny batches — smaller micro-batches for interactive streams. The trade-off is higher per-token compute cost. For Dedicated we can carve out low-latency lanes (reserved capacity) and also have a best-effort burst lane for throughput.
[03:10] Diego: What about fallback? If Dedicated is saturated, do you have automatic fallback to Hosted or smaller model variants? We need graceful degradation.
[03:16] Kamala: Yes — smart routing policy can fall back to compatible model variants, region failover, or degrade quality (e.g., reduce max tokens or use a quantized variant) depending on policy. We'll work with you to set thresholds for graceful fallback.
[03:29] Jonas: Can we get metrics at token-granularity? We need per-route p95, token/sec, per-model latencies, and cost breakdown.
[03:36] Sanjay: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, traces, and we can export logs to your observability stack. Retention is configurable (and an add-on for long-term storage).
[03:45] Evelyn: Security — SOC2 and ISO? Also SSO.
[03:48] Kamala: We are SOC 2 Type II compliant and have ISO alignment. For Private deployments you can use your KMS/HSM and our control plane integrates with SAML/SSO and can push audit logs to your SIEM. We'll follow up with the docs.
[03:59] Mira: Great. Let's get into the benchmark numbers you recommend. For our pilot we want to see: p95 first-token <= 350ms, steady-state token throughput of at least 600 tokens/sec per GPU for the 30B model, and 4 concurrent streams maintaining p95 <= 400ms. Is that realistic?
[04:16] Liam: For 30B on A100-style GPUs, 600 tokens/sec steady-state is achievable with quantization and optimized kernels. But first-token p95 — depends on the request path and KV cache warm state. On Dedicated, with pinned instances and prewarmed model, p95 first-token around 200–300ms is plausible. For Hosted, it can be more variable depending on load.
[04:33] Jonas: And what about peak bursts? We might get a surge of 20 concurrent quick queries in a region during large incidents. We need a burst plan — can Dedicated scale temporarily?
[04:42] Sanjay: Dedicated supports autoscaling and burst capacity options. There's a warm pool concept. For extremely short spikes we also recommend prefix/KV caching and fronting with a tiny distilled model to handle control-plane chatter.
[04:55] Diego: Network-wise, if we do Private in our VPC, is there any egress latency/handshake that would affect first-token?
[05:00] Liam: There is some network overhead but it's generally smaller than model compute. We'll coordinate with you on placement (same AZ preference) to reduce RTT. For Private on-prem, disk-backed model warm caches and persistent KV cache keep cold starts rare.
[05:13] Mira: Ok, experimental design — what do you want from us to run a meaningful benchmark?
[05:18] Kamala: We'll need representative prompts, a sample of conversation histories (context lengths), concurrency profile (arrival rate), target model config, and any constraints like VPC egress. We'll send a harness (script) that runs tokenized workloads and measures p50/p95/p99 for first-token and steady-state tokens/sec.
[05:31] Mira: We can supply prompts and 48 hours of anonymized chat logs to approximate context lengths.
[05:35] Kamala: Perfect. We'll provide an opinionated default load profile as well.
[05:39] Jonas: For measurement methodology — are you measuring p95 at application level (end-to-end including network) or just service-level (server-side)?
[05:45] Sanjay: By default our harness measures both: client-observed end-to-end and server-side generation latency. That helps isolate network vs compute.
[05:52] Evelyn: Cost question — can you give a rough unit cost for Hosted vs Dedicated for our expected load? Ballpark only.
[05:57] Kamala: Ballpark: Hosted per-token unit is higher, partly because of multi-tenant overhead and elastic infra. Dedicated monthly commit gives a much lower per-token effective cost if you sustain loads. We'll share a simple cost model with example numbers.
[06:08] Mira: We'd like to see cost vs latency curves — e.g., what does p95 look like when minimizing cost per token vs when prioritizing latency.
[06:15] Liam: We'll produce that with the benchmarks. We can also propose quantization profiles that hit certain cost/latency points.
[06:20] Diego: On the security side: for private deployment can you confirm KMS integration options and whether keys ever leave our control?
[06:26] Kamala: For Private, you manage KMS and keys never leave your environment. For Dedicated hosted in our cloud, we support customer-managed keys via a KMS bridge with strict access controls and audit logs. We'll include details in the security packet.
[06:39] Mira: How do rollouts work? If we pin a model version, can we do a canary to smaller percentage first?
[06:44] Sanjay: Yes — rollouts support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin to a model version and define thresholds (error rate, p95) to rollback automatically.
[06:54] Jonas: We care about KV cache invalidation semantics — if we update a model or change quantization, will cache mismatches cause incorrect outputs?
[06:59] Liam: Cache keys are bound to model id and tokenizer config. If you change model weights or tokenizer we recommend a cache flush. For some minor quantization changes we have compatibility modes but we'll test in the pilot.
[07:11] Evelyn: Ok let's talk pilot timeline. If we start next week can you do a dedicated trial for 2–3 days to prove p95 and token/sec metrics?
[07:19] Kamala: We can schedule a dedicated trial the week of 2027-11-08. The trial will run your workload on a reserved pool with controlled concurrency and streaming enabled.
[07:27] Mira: Perfect. What success criteria should we use to decide to go with Dedicated vs Private?
[07:31] Kamala: Suggested criteria: 1) p95 first-token <= 350ms for 4 concurrent heavy streams; 2) sustained token/sec meets your 600 tokens/sec baseline per GPU (or cost-effective equivalent); 3) clear security integration (KMS/SSO) validated; 4) predictable cost per-token within budget target. If Dedicated passes but you still require keys in VPC for compliance, we can move to Private next phase.
[07:50] Jonas: Can you run an escape velocity test for sudden contra — by that I mean a scenario where we throw 20 concurrent heavy streams and see fallback behavior?
[07:57] Sanjay: Yes — we'll include a surge scenario. We'll show how graceful degradation paths work: switch to quantized variant, reduce max tokens, or route to a distilled fallback model.
[08:07] Diego: For logging and observability, will we get traces per request with token boundaries?
[08:11] Liam: Yes — per-request traces, token timing breakdowns, and sampling options. You can also forward logs to Datadog/Elastic/Splunk.
[08:18] Mira: One last technical: do you support streaming with WebSocket + SSE or only chunked HTTP streaming? We prefer SSE for browser clients.
[08:24] Kamala: We support chunked HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket integrations. We'll include examples in the dev guide.
[08:30] Evelyn: Great. Any concerns on our side? Jonas?
[08:33] Jonas: Network constraints in two EU regions may complicate Private deployment. We'll follow up with Diego's topology.
[08:38] Diego: I'll share it. Also need to coordinate firewall rules for the Dedicated trial.
[08:42] Kamala: Ok noted. We'll include a checklist for firewall openings and port ranges.
[08:47] Mira: How frequent will billing snapshots be available during the trial? We want to estimate cost delta of low-latency lane vs best-effort throughput.
[08:54] Kamala: Real-time usage and cost are available in the Console; we can provide hourly cost estimates during the trial.
[08:59] Sanjay: One small note — for 30B models, tokenization strategy matters for tokens/sec. If you have heavy markdown or long history in prompts, per-token throughput can drop. We usually recommend truncating older context and using retrieval augmentation.
[09:12] Mira: Understood; we'll provide typical contexts.
[09:15] Kamala: Quick recap / commitments: we'll send the benchmark harness + sample load profile and a proposed schedule for the dedicated trial (week of 11/08). Liam will own the test harness. Kamala will draft pilot SoW and pricing. We'll also send security docs and SSO/KMS checklist.
[09:33] Evelyn: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side — we'll need to provision temporary credentials and open firewall rules for the trial. Diego will coordinate.
[09:40] Diego: Yep I'll follow up after the call.
[09:43] Kamala: Perfect. Anything else?
[09:45] Mira: Nope, that's it. Thanks all.
[09:47] Kamala: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

(End of recording)
